references.text: The house of Israel called the bread manna, and it was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.
Manna is described further: it was like coriander seed and looked like bdellium, and the people gathered it and ground it.
Moses reminds the people that God humbled them and let them hunger, then gave them manna to eat, which neither they nor their fathers had known.
God gave them manna in the wilderness, which their fathers did not know, to humble and test them.
The manna stopped the day after they ate from the produce of the land, and the Israelites no longer received manna.
God rained down manna for them as food and gave them grain from heaven; people ate the bread of angels.
The people prayed, and God sent quails and satisfied them with bread from heaven.
Jesus refers to the manna when the Jews say: 'Our fathers ate manna in the wilderness, as it is written: He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'
Jesus compares himself to the manna and says that he is the bread of life coming down from heaven, unlike the manna which their fathers ate and yet died.
Paul writes that all the fathers ate the same spiritual food, referring to the manna in the wilderness.
The ark of the covenant contained a golden jar with manna, as a testimony to God's provision in the wilderness.
Jesus promises the one who overcomes to give some of the hidden manna, a spiritual blessing that points back to the manna in the wilderness.
Moses' explanation of what the manna is is followed directly by the command to preserve this bread as a testimony for future generations.
Moses' explanation in verse 15 about the bread from the Lord finds its context in verse 8, where he reminds the people that the gift was an answer to their complaints.
Verse 4 describes the divine planning that directly leads to the event and reaction described in verse 15.
Jesus uses the manna event (v. 15) as a typological precursor to reveal himself as the true bread from heaven.
The manna (v. 15) serves as a clear precursor to the bread of the Lord's Supper (Mark), where Christ is the true bread from heaven.
